## Verification of 780840b (organization lookup guard)

- **Guard is semantically exact.** `canAccessInviteOnlyTarget` returns false immediately when `userId` is absent, and only consults `userOrganizationIds` on the `ownerScope === "organization"` branch. The new condition `session && row.owner_scope === "organization"` (`src/lib/server/reader-views.ts:218`) therefore skips the membership query in precisely the cases where its result could never change the outcome. Owner match, allowlist, and moderation overrides are still evaluated for user-scoped targets.
- **No auth widening.** An empty array is passed in the skipped cases, which is the same value an unaffiliated user would have produced. The "user stranger with matching organization ID" test pins the important negative: a user whose org list happens to contain the owner's user ID is still refused for a user-scoped target.
- **Session lookup unchanged.** `getRequestSession` still runs for every invite-only request, so the hot path saves one `member` query per request, nothing more.
- **Tests.** Six scope/membership combinations run against both `view` and `count`, asserting status, the returned total, buffer `add` calls, and that the organization lookup is invoked only for organization-owned targets. The `afterEach` restores the `Pool.prototype.query` spy so it cannot leak into other suites.
- **Prior finding #5** (inline SQL assembly in `handleReaderViews`) is untouched and remains a P3 style observation, not a blocker.

items.title: The scaffold's keydown handler now routes through `ignoreReaderShortcut`, which rejects `event
items.body: The scaffold's keydown handler now routes through `ignoreReaderShortcut`, which rejects `event.repeat`. That was specified for Shift+Y, but it also applies to `j`/`k`/`h`/`o`/`/`, so holding `j` to step through notes no longer repeats. Spec says "Preserve existing reader navigation keys".
items.suggestion: Either accept and document, or apply the repeat/modifier filter only in the Shift+Y handler and keep the original typing-context check for navigation keys.

items.title: fn-153 and fn-155 shipped both `db/schema
items.body: fn-153 and fn-155 shipped both `db/schema.sql` changes and a `db/migrations/<n>.sql`; this change only updates `schema.sql`. Bootstrap applies `schema.sql` at startup so production is covered, but the runbook convention for controlled migration is not followed.

items.title: A protected `definition` node (e
items.body: A protected `definition` node (e.g. `[private]: https://gno.sh/secret/...`) is rewritten into a root-level `text` node with the value `[Nonportable link omitted]`, since definitions have no children. remark-stringify emits it as its own paragraph (`\[Nonportable link omitted]`), so the copied document ends with an orphan placeholder line unrelated to any inline reference. Unprotected definitions are also kept even though every `linkReference` has already been inlined, producing duplicate link data. The test only asserts absence of the token, not absence of the stray line.
items.suggestion: After inlining references, drop `definition` nodes from `tree.children` entirely instead of converting them to text.

items.title: Each displayed note fires `view`, an immediate `count`, and a second `count` at 5
items.body: Each displayed note fires `view`, an immediate `count`, and a second `count` at 5.5 s. Each request resolves the target with a multi-join query on the analytics pool (`max: 2`, 1 s connect timeout). Under moderate concurrency the pool queue will hit the timeout and return 503, which is safe for reading but wastes work; the delayed re-count only exists to show the reader their own increment.
items.suggestion: Return the current total in the `view` 202 body and drop the delayed re-count, or keep a single `count` request. Not a blocker; the failure path is already non-blocking.
